referents.why: Second person masculine singular inside the speech Moses is told to say to Pharaoh ('go to Pharaoh and say to him'); the 'you' of that speech is its addressee, Pharaoh.
referents.category: second person inside a commanded speech

referents.why: First person singular inside the speech introduced by 'thus says Yahweh'; the 'I' of that speech is its speaker, the LORD, whom Moses is to quote.
referents.category: first person inside a messenger-formula speech

referents.why: Second person masculine singular suffix on 'territory'; same speech, so the addressee, Pharaoh. The host noun w11 is the possessed thing, not the referent.
referents.category: second person inside a commanded speech

links.why: The infinitive 'to let go' completes the main verb 'refuse' (a verb of refusing); it is what is refused, not an aim of the refusing.

The conditional is real: the אִם clause 'you refuse' is the condition and the 'behold, I am striking' clause is what it conditions; the host is the next clause after the condition that is not an infinitive complement.
The waw in וְאִם opens the verse, joining it to the speech before; there is no separate-word waw between cl0 and cl2, and the pair is already linked as condition and consequence by 'if'.
links.category: conjunction of the conditional read as a plain and

links.why: No conjunction stands between the particle הִנֵּה and its participle; the waw is on the particle, before cl2. cl2 and cl3 are one clause the parser split, so the participle is the particle's predicate, not a second 'and' clause.
links.category: presentative particle split from its predicate

links.why: The infinitive clause 'to let (them) go' is the complement filling the object role of the participle 'refusing'.
links.category: infinitive complement of a verb of refusing

groups.why: The if-clause is cl0 (cl1 sits inside it). The consequence is 'behold, I am about to strike ...': the particle הִנֵּה (cl2) is the head of a presentative clause whose predicate is the participle (cl3), so the consequence is both together, not cl2 alone, which is only the particle.
groups.category: consequence split across a particle and its predicate

none_fit.what: The presentative particle הִנֵּה ('behold') and the participle that is its predicate are one clause that the parser split in two; no link type joins a particle clause to its predicate (and is wrong, within is for role-nesting).

none_fit.where: the verse as a whole and Exo.7.26#turn1
none_fit.what: This verse plainly continues the speech Moses is to say to Pharaoh (the LORD's message begun in 8:1), but the turn group of the earlier verse cannot be given a further part from here, and a new turn here would have no saying clause as frame. The continuation of one speech across a verse boundary has no form among the group kinds.

cant_tell.what: The direction of the builder's if link (cl0 -if-> cl2)
cant_tell.why: link_types says the condition is the destination and the conditioned clause is the source, which would give cl2 -if-> cl0; the builder writes it the other way. Kept as built because the pairing is right and the conditional group carries the roles explicitly.
